questions.question: What is AWS CloudTrail?
options: A web service that uses log files to record Amazon Web Service (AWS) events
A web service that controls other Amazon Web Services (AWS) services through application programming interface (API) calls
A web service that manages users and permissions
A web service that assesses application vulnerabilities
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) A web service that uses log files to record Amazon Web Service (AWS) events

• Why it's correct: "A web service that uses log files to record Amazon Web Service (AWS) events" is the accurate response for this question. In the context of "What is AWS CloudTrail?", this option aligns directly with the official curriculum specifications and technical requirements.

• Architectural Context: AWS CloudTrail is an auditing, compliance, and governance service that records all API activity and management events in your AWS account. Every request made via the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or SDKs is logged with the caller identity, timestamp, source IP address, and request parameters, and delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket.

• Exam Takeaway: CloudTrail = Auditing & API History ('Who did what, when, and from where'). Distinguish from CloudWatch (monitoring metrics) and AWS Config (configuration state).
